ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 Revision, effective January 1, 2025); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information of Legal Persons and Other Organizations (Joint Order No. 3 [2024] of the People's Bank of China and the State Administration for Market Regulation, effective November 1, 2024); Administrative Measures for Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing of Financial Institutions (PBOC Order No. 3 [2016], as amended); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective July 1, 2024).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of Taiwan Parent Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille not applicable because Taiwan is not a contracting party to the Hague Apostille Convention; use parallel Consular Legalization path only: Taiwan notary public notarization, then verification by the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF), then transmission through the Chinese Notary Association (CNA) for cross-strait document authentication and local administrative recognition.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of Taiwan Parent Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille not applicable; Consular Legalization only: notarize the certificate before a Taiwan district court or notary office, submit to SEF for verification, forward to CNA for cross-strait notarized document exchange, and thereafter present the verified copy to the relevant Chinese SAMR and bank compliance departments.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney Executed by Taiwan Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Parent Investor Board of Directors and Taiwan Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille not applicable; Consular Legalization only: original board resolution notarized by a Taiwan notary, authenticated by SEF, forwarded to CNA, then accepted by Chinese authorities in connection with the WFOE incorporation filing.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of Taiwan Parent Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs Certified Copy or Taiwan Company Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille not applicable; Consular Legalization only: certified copy notarized in Taiwan, verified by SEF, transmitted through CNA, and thereafter recognized as lawful evidence for UBO and incorporation due diligence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Taiwan Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille not applicable; Consular Legalization only: bank officer's signature and seal notarized by a Taiwan notary, SEF verification and CNA transmission of the notarized copy; the original bank letter must not be apostilled or mixed with any Hague process.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists, the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctions list, and the People's Bank of China anti-money laundering blacklist. Enhanced due diligence is required for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), foreign PEPs, and international organization PEPs, including source-of-wealth verification, beneficial ownership chain re-identification, ongoing transaction monitoring, and immediate filing of suspicious transaction reports (STRs) to the China Anti-Money Laundering Monitoring and Analysis Center (CAMLMAC). Domestic screening must also cover the provisions of the Administrative Measures on Beneficial Owner Information, including identification and verification of ultimate natural persons holding 25% or more equity or control rights.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Name Declaration System (national integrated online enterprise service platform, including provincial SAMR portals)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: WFOE statutory names must be in Simplified Chinese; an English name may be registered as a secondary name but is not the legal name. The name must follow the four-tier naming structure: administrative division plus distinctive trade name plus industry or operating characteristic plus company type. The distinctive name may use the transliterated Chinese rendering of the foreign shareholder's corporate name; pinyin or Roman characters are not permitted in the core Chinese statutory name unless used as the separate English company name. Any territorial qualifier including words referring to Taiwan, China, Chinese, or national status requires special ministerial approval. Phonetic transliteration must avoid misleading similarity with prohibited or sensitive tokens and comply with the Administrative Provisions on Enterprise Name Registration.

stage_1.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of the name declaration, the applicant may submit to the same SAMR portal a new declaration with revised components, or apply in writing for reconsideration to the SAMR at the next higher level or to the same-level people's government under the Administrative Reconsideration Law of the People's Republic of China. The appeal must be filed within 60 days of the written rejection notice and should identify the examination reference number, the rejected name, the statutory basis for the proposed name, and any supporting documents showing no conflict with existing names or prohibited tokens. Legal counsel must preserve all rejection records and submit any administrative appeal within the statutory window.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (as amended), particularly Articles 1, 2, 6, 8, 128, 129, 130, 156, 161, 171, 172, 178, 192, 208, 210, 216, 218 and 221; Foreign Investment Act, Articles 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 and 9; Regulations for Investment by Foreign Nationals; and Central Bank of Taiwan foreign exchange reporting guidance.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan; Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs for foreign-investment approval and licensing; National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance for post-incorporation tax registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application Form under Article 6 of the Taiwan Company Act, accompanied by Articles of Incorporation, first board resolution minutes, paid-in capital certificate, registered office lease, and the Foreign Investment Approval Certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is imposed by the Taiwan Company Act for a limited liability company. However, the Investment Commission, in granting foreign investment approval, will require the approved investment amount to be fully remitted into a dedicated New Taiwan Dollar capital contribution account in the company's name and held there until incorporation is completed. The funds shall not be diverted or withdrawn before the issuance of the Company Registration Certificate unless permitted by the Investment Commission or Central Bank rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS MEETING OF [Company] LIMITED. A special meeting of the Board of Directors of [Company] Limited was duly convened and held on [date] at [address] with proper notice given to all directors pursuant to Article 172 of the Taiwan Company Act. The following directors were present in person and constituted a quorum: [Director A], [Director B], [Director C]. The Chairman presided over the meeting and the Corporate Secretary recorded the minutes. WHEREAS, the Company is a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company to be incorporated under the Taiwan Company Act and the Foreign Investment Act; and WHEREAS, the Company intends to engage in lawful professional consulting services relating to international anti-dumping inquiries, trade remedy defense, accounting support, and associated advisory services. NOW, THEREFORE, the Board unanimously resolves as follows: 1. Subscription and Issue of Share Capital. The initial share capital is [amount] New Taiwan Dollars, divided into [number] ordinary shares having a par value of [par value] New Taiwan Dollars per share. The sole foreign shareholder subscribes for all issued shares and shall pay the full subscription amount in cash into a dedicated capital contribution account before filing for company registration. No redemption, set-off, or withdrawal of the subscribed capital is permitted unless authorized by law. 2. Banking Authorization. The Company shall open general deposit and operational accounts with [Bank Name]. The Chairman, the General Manager, and the Chief Financial Officer, acting jointly in any two signatures, are hereby authorized to execute all account opening forms, signatory registrations, wire transfer instructions, foreign exchange declarations, and any other banking documents. All disbursements shall be limited to bona fide corporate purposes. 3. Registered Office. The registered office of the Company is fixed at [address], Taiwan. The Board approves the adoption of that address as the statutory registered office and instructs the Corporate Secretary to record it with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and maintain the statutory corporate registers there. 4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. [Person A] is appointed Chairman and Chief Executive Officer; [Person B] is appointed General Manager; [Person C] is appointed Corporate Secretary; and [Person D] is appointed Chief Financial Officer. Each appointed officer accepts the office and shall exercise all powers and perform all duties delegated under the Articles of Incorporation and applicable law. 5. Filing and Implementation. The Chairman and the Corporate Secretary, jointly, are authorized to prepare, execute, notarize, and file all documents necessary for statutory incorporation, tax registration, social insurance registration, and trade remedy licensing, and to retain counsel, chartered accountants, and consultants as needed. There being no further business, the meeting was duly adjourned. [Signature Block]

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA), accessible through the China Electronic Tax Administration (e-Tax Bureau) electronic portal at https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn and the STA official portal at http://www.chinatax.gov.cn
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Under the PRC multi-license integration reform, a WFOE must first be incorporated with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR). SAMR issues the Business License carrying an 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is automatically recognized by the State Taxation Administration as the taxpayer identification number for enterprise income tax, VAT, and all other PRC taxes. The WFOE then completes tax registration through the China Electronic Tax Administration (e-Tax Bureau), is assigned to a competent tax office, files its accounting and financial system records, and obtains a digital invoice issuance quota on the STA Electronic Invoice Service Platform. For a foreign non-resident enterprise that does not establish a mainland China entity, the competent tax authority requires non-resident tax record filing through the e-Tax Bureau and may allocate a non-resident taxpayer code for withholding-at-source obligations; no separate VAT identification number is issued unless the non-resident makes taxable supplies requiring VAT registration. All statutory filings are conducted through the official e-Tax Bureau and, where customs clearance is required, the China International Trade Single Window.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The People's Republic of China does not operate a check-the-box election or elective pass-through classification regime. A WFOE is automatically taxed as a resident enterprise on its worldwide income. Hybrid mismatch treatment is not elective; anti-avoidance rules apply under the enterprise income tax framework.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory VAT general taxpayer registration applies when annual taxable sales exceed CNY 5,000,000. Newly established WFOEs must complete VAT registration immediately upon tax registration regardless of turnover; below the threshold they may be classified as small-scale taxpayers, with an applicable statutory rate of 3% currently reduced to 1% under the existing temporary concession, and small-scale taxpayers may benefit from a temporary monthly sales exemption of up to CNY 100,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The STA Electronic Invoice Service Platform requires real-time issuance and upload of fully digitalised electronic invoices in OFD format. The Golden Tax System Phase IV fiscally validates each invoice through a mandatory anti-fraud digital stamp and tax-control code before the invoice may be delivered to the buyer. Domestic and export B2B invoices must carry the buyer tax identification number and are synchronised into the buyer's e-Tax Bureau file. The e-Tax Bureau and China International Trade Single Window interoperate for electronic customs export declarations and export tax refund/exemption applications.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under PRC VAT law as reflected in Caishui [2016] No. 36 and subsequent administrative announcements, exported goods qualify for zero VAT rating when the goods are actually declared to and physically leave mainland Chinese customs territory, the exporter issues an export invoice, the foreign exchange is received from the overseas buyer through banking channels, and the export tax refund/exemption declaration is electronically filed. Qualifying cross-border services listed by the STA as zero-rated, such as international transport, R&D and technology services, software services, design services, information system services, and business process management services, may also qualify for zero-rating where the recipient is an overseas enterprise or individual and the services are not consumed in mainland China. The target WFOE's anti-dumping trade-remedy defense and legal/accounting consulting services are normally VAT-exempt rather than zero-rated under the cross-border exemption catalogue when all conditions are met, and therefore must not improperly claim a refund of input VAT as if zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic Customs Export Declaration issued through the China International Trade Single Window (the official export declaration for goods)
Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document such as air waybill, railway consignment note, or CMR road consignment note
Commercial invoice and detailed packing list
Export sales contract or purchase order indicating the foreign buyer, Incoterms, and value of export goods

Bank SWIFT credit advice and SAFE Trade Monitoring System record evidencing receipt and verification of export proceeds (the functional replacement for an Inward Remittance Certificate; FIRC is not a mainland China statutory document)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to post-export audit by the STA. Failure to substantiate physical export, overseas receipt, or statutory documentation within the prescribed 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation period will result in reversal of the 0% rating, supplementary VAT at the applicable domestic rate depending on the supply, late payment surcharge at 0.05% per day, and administrative penalties under the Tax Administration Law of the People's Republic of China. Fraudulent export refund claims may attract penalties of up to five times the refund obtained, recovery of clawed-back refunds, and criminal liability under Article 204 of the Criminal Law for fraudulent export-tax-rebate offences, including imprisonment and confiscation of assets. The State Administration of Foreign Exchange may also downgrade the exporter's trade credit classification, triggering enhanced supervision, documentary examination, and cash deposit requirements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) under the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act administered jointly with the Financial Supervisory Commission
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Taiwan operates a managed floating exchange rate regime with full current account convertibility and a controlled capital account. New Taiwan Dollar (TWD) convertibility is unrestricted for trade-related payments such as import settlement, service fees, royalties, and dividend remittances that have been duly approved under the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment injections, loan repayments, and portfolio remittances, require prior approval from the Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) or a designated foreign exchange bank acting within delegated authority. Export proceeds are generally free from forced conversion but must be repatriated to Taiwan and reported through the prescribed foreign exchange declaration system. Profit remittance by a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) requires a certified capital verification report, audited financial statements, and proof of tax clearance, with the central bank monitoring for disguised capital movements. Surrender requirements are effectively relaxed for exporters, yet the settlement of foreign exchange receipts is mandatory. Structural hurdles include the need to evidence economic substance, comply with annual reporting obligations, and ensure that all cross-border payments pass through approved FX banks to avoid fines or suspension of foreign currency accounts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export foreign currency receipts must be repatriated to a designated foreign exchange bank within five business days from the date of collection, and while full conversion to TWD is not statutorily mandatory, the exporter must complete the Central Bank's foreign exchange declaration and can hold the proceeds in a foreign currency deposit account; failure to repatriate within the timeline requires prior approval and documented justification.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account / Foreign Currency Deposit Account
Basic Operational Currency Account / Foreign Currency Deposit Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI solutions are legally constrained in Taiwan because a non-bank fintech entity cannot independently hold corporate operational funds in TWD or provide TWD-denominated accounts without a banking license. Foreign fintech EMIs offering multi-currency accounts largely rely on partner banks and would not satisfy the Central Bank's requirement for local banking supervision over the WFOE's primary treasury flows. These EMIs may be used only as auxiliary payment appliances for receiving small international trade remittances, subject to the underlying designated FX bank remaining the settlement and compliance anchor; however, any attempt to operate a treasury account through an unlicensed EMI as the main clearing rail is legally barred and carries regulatory risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory company responsible person and the beneficial controller must physically appear in-branch at a designated Tier-1 commercial bank in Taiwan for the initial KYC interview and account activation; remote consular proxy opening is not permitted for a standard corporate account, although a locally appointed non-resident director may complete the interview through a certified representative only when the bank grants exceptional case-by-case approval and conducts video verification with the foreign executive.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner transparency deficiency where the mainland Chinese parent holds ownership in a Taiwan-registered WFOE, raising cross-strait financial secrecy concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified audited shareholding charts, notarized certificates of incorporation of both the parent and Taiwan subsidiary, board resolution naming the UBO, signed UBO declarations with passport copies, and a fully completed beneficial ownership register with explanation of any indirect nominees or trust layers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between the stated business scope of anti-dumping legal advisory services and the actual flow of funds, since management consulting fees may be used to shift earnings out of Taiwan
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed client engagement contracts, service delivery timelines, proof of staff localization in Taiwan, tax filing receipts for revenue, invoices issued under the Taiwan entity's Uniform Invoice system, and an annual compliance undertaking describing the anti-dumping advisory workflow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Concern about foreign exchange declaration compliance on inbound capital injection and subsequent dividend repatriation, especially under the Central Bank's monitoring systems
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved investment application from the Investment Commission, bank remittance advice showing purpose code '370' or equivalent FDI coding, capital verification certificate from a Taiwan CPA, and stamp-verified prior year audited statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential nexus with high-risk cross-border payments due to the nature of legal defense services for Chinese exporting clients facing anti-dumping measures, which may be interpreted as politically exposed advisory activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening report confirming that no client appears on Chinese, Taiwanese, or international sanctions lists, business references from two independent Taiwan commercial banks, a senior management SOI statement, and a KYC questionnaire detailing each client's ultimate purpose of engagement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital from the mainland Chinese parent must be remitted via SWIFT with the purpose code clearly indicating direct investment, followed by submission of the investment approval letter issued by the Taiwan Investment Commission to the designated FX bank. The bank will file the foreign exchange declaration with the Central Bank, and the funds will be deposited into the capital escrow account. Once the CPA issues the capital verification report and the company completes business registration changes, the capital can be transferred into the operational TWD account for lawful business use.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade-related settlements arising from anti-dumping defense services, the WFOE should use SWIFT MT103 for straightforward cross-border fee settlements to overseas law firms and consultants. Commercial letters of credit are appropriate only if the entity also engages in physical goods transactions; documentary collections serve as a secondary rail for lower-value, relationship-based trade flows. All outbound disbursements must be supported by signed advisory contracts, tax invoices, and remittance reason codes, and are routed through the designated FX bank to satisfy the Central Bank's monitoring and anti-money-laundering reporting requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: TWD/USD and TWD/CNY forward exchange contracts for hedge ratios not exceeding 100% of underlying trade or receivable exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on TWD only through authorized foreign banks for offshore risk management, subject to Central Bank prohibitions against speculative NDF positions
Currency swaps which are permitted primarily for investment-related debt service and cross-border capital flows, with bank approval required and no zero-coupon swap structures allowed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Credit Information Report (Enterprise Annual Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) of the People's Republic of China through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from January 1 through June 30; report data as at December 31 of the preceding tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If filed after June 30 or not filed, the WFOE is placed on the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operation; where correction is not made within 3 years, it is transferred to the List of Enterprises with Serious Illegal and Dishonest Acts, triggering public credit deterioration, market-access restrictions, restrictions on bank credit and administrative changes, and possible revocation of the business license for persistent non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Information Report (Foreign Investment Annual Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce of the People's Republic of China (MOFCOM) in coordination with SAMR through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from January 1 through June 30 for information as at December 31 of the preceding year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The commerce department orders rectification for a prescribed period; failure to rectify or submission of false information may incur an administrative fine of RMB 100,000 to RMB 500,000, negative corporate credit record, and suspension of foreign-invested preferential procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual FDI Stock and Equity Information Registration (FDI Stock-Equity Register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange of the People's Republic of China (SAFE) through the banking channel or local SAFE branch
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before June 30 for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to complete the annual FDI registration impedes all foreign-exchange transactions with the Chinese entity, including dividend remittance, profit repatriation, cross-border lending, capital account payments and transfer of equity; the WFOE may be listed as non-compliant by SAFE and subjected to administrative penalties for unauthorized foreign-exchange operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Settlement Filing (Annual CIT Return and Self-Assessment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA) local in-charge tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filing and settlement on or before May 31 of the year following each tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts an administrative penalty of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 (or RMB 2,000 to RMB 50,000 in serious cases), a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% on the unpaid corporate income tax, and potential tax audit and assessment of income; false or evasive filing may be penalized at 0.5 to 5 times the underpaid tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Information Confirmation and Change Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) together with the People's Bank of China (PBOC) under the Beneficial Ownership Information Management Measures
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation within the January 1 through June 30 enterprise annual report cycle; any change in beneficial owners, shareholder structure, or control chain must be filed within 30 days of the occurrence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False, incomplete, or overdue beneficial ownership reports expose the WFOE to SAMR rectification orders and administrative fines, adverse credit records, restrictions on registration changes, and in serious cases penalties on responsible persons under the beneficial-ownership regime.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Financial Statements, CPA Audit Report and Shareholders' Approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting and shareholders of the WFOE; the audited financial statements must also be available to SAMR, the tax authority, and SAFE upon request or in support of annual filings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Preparation within 4 months after year-end and finalization before the annual shareholders' meeting; for practical statutory linkage, the audit should be completed on or before May 31, with annual financial statements delivered to shareholders at least 20 days before the annual meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Without a CPA audit report, the WFOE cannot consistently complete its enterprise credit annual report, tax reconciliation, or foreign-exchange stock equity registration; this exposes directors and shareholders to corporate governance liability, loss of audit-evidence reliability for profit distribution, and may trigger SAMR or tax authority fines where audited financial statements are legally required.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A PRC Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise has no quantitative turnover, balance-sheet, or headcount exemption from annual audit: under Article 164 of the PRC Company Law, every company must prepare annual financial reports and have them audited by an accounting firm formed under PRC law. The audit obligation exists irrespective of whether total assets, revenue, or employee count are below RMB 10 million, RMB 30 million, or 50 persons. Additional mandatory audit and filing duties apply if the WFOE is an issuer on a securities exchange, is a financial institution under PBOC, CBIRC, or CSRC supervision, is controlling a significant merger or investment under MOFCOM rules, or is treated as a large state-influenced enterprise under SASAC guidelines; for such regulated entities, statutory audit is triggered at any size, and public issuers must additionally file audited reports under the PRC Securities Law and CSRC rules. In practical administration, SAMR, tax authorities, and SAFE may require the audited financial statements as a supporting document for annual credit filing, annual income tax settlement, and annual FDI stock and equity registration.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS/ASBE), which are substantially converged with IFRS, apply to the WFOE's statutory books and standalone financial statements. Eligible small-scale enterprises may elect the PRC Small Enterprise Accounting Standards where permitted, but WFOEs engaged in trade-remedy defense consulting with foreign capital, cross-border payments, and licensing requirements should apply full CAS. For the overseas parent in the Taiwan jurisdiction, separate consolidation under IFRS may be required, but all filings to SAMR, MOFCOM, SAFE, and the STA must be derived from the PRC-statutory CAS financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The WFOE must file initial beneficial ownership information with SAMR under the PRC Beneficial Ownership Information Management Measures. Thereafter, each annual enterprise credit report filed between January 1 and June 30 operates as the annual confirmation of the register of beneficial owners, shareholders, and ultimate controlling parties. Any direct or indirect shareholding transfer, change of control, change of ultimate beneficial owner, or change in the chain of ownership must be reported to SAMR within 30 days from the date on which the change occurs; annual confirmation does not eliminate the need for event-driven 30-day filings. Failure to file an event-driven update on time may expose the WFOE to penalties even if the later annual confirmation is accurate.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders register with contribution amounts, contributions made, and share transfer history)
Register of Directors (director identity, term, and appointment/removal records)
Register of Charges / Mortgages (records of security, pledge of equity, and registered charges over assets where applicable)
Minute Book (authenticated minutes of shareholders' resolutions and board resolutions)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 20% statutory rate is reduced by the 15% research and development investment tax credit under the Statute for Industrial Innovation, and by qualifying free-trade-zone incentives for cross-border trade-defense support services; the Basic Tax Act alternative minimum tax imposes an effective floor of 12% on preferential income, and undistributed earnings are additionally subject to a 5% retained-earnings surtax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Settlement Return Form 101, filed through the Taiwan Ministry of Finance Taxation Portal electronic filing system using the company ROC tax identification number.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual settlement return with provisional tax payment obligation during the year; provisional payment due 30 September and annual filing due 31 May.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year taxpayer, the annual return must be filed and the tax paid between 1 May and 31 May of the following year; for a fiscal-year taxpayer, the return is due within the fifth month after fiscal year-end. Provisional income tax returns for the current year are due by 30 September.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identity, ROC tax ID, industry classification ISIC 7490, paid-in capital, authorized business scope, and complete register of shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All non-resident shareholders must be itemized in the non-resident ownership schedule. If any mainland China person or mainland China enterprise holds 25% or more, the application of the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement must be reported so that reduced dividend withholding rates can be documented contemporaneously.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross annual revenue from anti-dumping trade-defense consulting, legal advocacy, government liaison work, expert testimony, case-management fees, and reimbursable litigation costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Revenue derived from legal or investigative work physically performed outside Taiwan for a non-resident client should be classified as Taiwan-source services if a Taiwanese office, employees, and decision-making produce the value; misclassification invites reassessment and withholding tax exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book-to-tax reconciliation: statutory and accounting income differences, disallowed expenses, exempt income, entertainment expenses, depreciation, and provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fees paid to non-resident law firms, expert witnesses, or affiliated trade-defense consultants are deductible only if the service was actually rendered, the payment is arm's length, and proper withholding has been made. Payments to mainland China service providers must be scrutinized under the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement and transfer pricing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transaction schedule and transfer pricing report attachment, including intra-group service fees, royalties, management charges, intercompany loans, and cross-border cost-sharing arrangements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Taiwan WFOE must disclose every related-party transaction with its non-resident parent or affiliates, apply the most appropriate arm's length method, and attach a Local File if aggregate related-party transactions exceed TWD 200 million. A Master File is additionally required when the group consolidated revenue exceeds TWD 30 billion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating loss carryforward deduction and calculation of available losses within the statutory carryforward period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses may be carried forward for ten years, but only if the Taiwan entity has real economic substance and the loss is not the product of inflated intra-group payments. Losses generated by a shell structure are disallowed and may trigger CFC or actual-management-place recharacterization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation, application of the 20% rate, alternative minimum tax calculation at 12%, credits, and final self-assessed tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax credits must be supported by documentation and apportioned to Taiwan-connected income. A mainland China shareholder resident may claim foreign tax credit relief under the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement only for income that is also taxed in mainland China and only with a valid Tax Residency Certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Undistributed retained earnings, legal reserves, distributable surplus, and reconciliation with any actual dividend distribution to foreign shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If dividends have actually been distributed to a non-resident shareholder, the 21% withholding tax is due and must be deposited using the withholding agent system. The annual return must be consistent with the withholding statements and beneficial ownership declarations filed for the distribution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing is penalized under Income Tax Act Article 108 at 3% of the unpaid tax for each two-month period of delay, up to 9%, increasing to 5% per two-month period up to 15% if the return remains unfiled after official notice. Late payment attracts interest and enforcement surcharges; underreporting exposes the taxpayer to a penalty of one to three times the underpaid tax under Article 110, and willful tax evasion opens criminal liability under Article 41 of the Tax Collection Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on dividends paid to a non-resident corporate or individual shareholder of a Taiwan profit-seeking enterprise, unless a treaty or the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement reduces the rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced dividend withholding rate under the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement, the non-resident beneficial owner must obtain an official Tax Residency Certificate from the mainland China tax authority, provide a beneficial ownership declaration, prove the minimum shareholding period, and submit the application through the Taiwan withholding agent before or at the time of payment. The withholding agent must retain board minutes, audited financial statements, shareholding registers, and bank payment records to evidence the claim; if reduced withholding is denied, a claim for refund must be filed within five years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax rates are 20% for royalties and 15% for interest paid to a non-resident without a Taiwan permanent establishment. Under the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement, royalties and interest beneficially owned by a mainland China resident may be taxable at 7%, provided the recipient satisfies economic substance, beneficial ownership, and residency certification requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Local File transfer pricing report is mandatory when aggregate related-party transactions of the Taiwan entity exceed TWD 200 million; a Master File is mandatory when the worldwide group consolidated revenue exceeds TWD 30 billion; Country-by-Country Report obligations arise when group revenue exceeds TWD 27 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan applies the economic substance doctrine through Income Tax Act Articles 43-3 and 43-4 for controlled foreign companies and actual management places, and through Article 12-1 of the Tax Collection Act which allows the tax authority to disregard transactions with no substantial commercial purpose. The Taiwan WFOE must demonstrate that core income-generating activities for anti-dumping trade defense, including case strategy, legal drafting, negotiation, contract execution, invoicing, and dispute management, are physically and economically performed in Taiwan, with real office space, qualified employees, and independent board decision-making.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating anti-dumping defense consulting revenue, creating fictitious invoices from shell vendors, destroying accounting records, or making false declarations to reduce the Taiwan profit-seeking enterprise tax liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act Article 110 imposes an administrative penalty of one to three times the underpaid tax plus interest; Tax Collection Act Article 41 imposes criminal liability of imprisonment for up to five years, short-term detention, and a fine of up to TWD 6,000,000 for fraudulent tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Company Act Article 23 and Civil Code Article 28, a director who approves fraudulent returns is jointly and severally liable for the company tax deficiency and damages to creditors and shareholders. Tax authorities may attach personal assets, seek court-ordered travel bans, blacklist the individual, and upon criminal conviction impose imprisonment and director disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Thin Capitalization
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using excessive intercompany loans, inflated management charges, or sham royalty payments to shift taxable profits out of Taiwan to the mainland China parent or another offshore affiliate without contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation and arm's length benchmarking.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act Articles 43-1 and 43-2 authorize adjustment of taxable income to arm's length and disallowance of excess interest expense. Failure to produce the required Local File or Master File may result in a deemed assessment, a penalty of one to three times the resulting tax deficiency under Article 110, and withholding tax recharacterization of disguised profit distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer pricing statements may be held personally liable for the adjusted tax amount under the doctrine of piercing the corporate veil. The director can face civil asset restitution, personal bank account seizure, blacklisting, travel restrictions, and criminal charges under Tax Collection Act Article 41 if the pricing scheme is found to be fraudulent rather than merely aggressive.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Money Laundering Compliance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Taiwan WFOE as a brass-plate entity with no office, no employees, and no board activity, while using it to route trade-defense advocacy commissions and suspicious wire transfers to third-country accounts or to fraudulently claim treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act Articles 43-3 and 43-4 allow the tax authority to disregard the entity and attribute income to the actual beneficial owner; Money Laundering Control Act Articles 6 and 7 impose registration, customer due diligence, and suspicious transaction reporting obligations; violations carry administrative fines and, for willful money laundering conduct, imprisonment for up to five years and fines up to TWD 15,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced when the shell entity is used as an instrument of illegality, making directors jointly and severally liable for company debts and tax liabilities. Directors can be blacklisted, prevented from leaving Taiwan, personally assessed for restitution, and imprisoned for money laundering complicity; the company may also be struck off and directors banned from serving as officers in Taiwan.
